value: US Government-sponsored work (US State Department IAA S-OES-07-IAA-0007; DOE contract DE-AC02-05CH11231), prepared by LBNL and AISI; no licence stated. Treat as public-domain-like government report but check before redistributing text/figures (many sheets excerpt vendor material).

Asia Pacific Partnership for Clean Development and Climate (2010). The State-of-the-Art Clean Technologies (SOACT) for Steelmaking Handbook, 2nd Edition. Prepared by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and American Iron and Steel Institute for the APP, US Department of State and US Department of Energy. December 2010. https://international.lbl.gov/publications/the-state-of-the-art-clean-technologies-soact-for-steelmaking-handbook-2nd-edition

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 15). The handbook is a catalogue of ~95 technology sheets, almost all measures on existing plants; their savings, costs and paybacks are in _measures (42 rows, not loaded). Main file: 19 whole technologies (alternative ironmaking processes, SCOPE21 and heat-recovery coke ovens, ECOARC, primary-energy melter, Castrip, thin-slab casting, off-gas combined cycle, COG hydrogen PSA) each with description and printed commercial status; the only absolute technology values are ECOARC 200 kWh/t, FASTMET NOx/PM, Finex and rotary-kiln capacities, PSH/Corex/Midrex CO2 reductions, Midrex CO2 removal 250 kg/t DRI, and the off-gas turbine 33% efficiency and 1090 USD/kWe. Flows: heat-recovery coke electricity export, rotary-kiln coal, ECOARC electrodes. No TRLs or whole-plant capex per t capacity are printed. Appendices 1-2 listed in the contents are not in this PDF. Stem/source-id chosen from the APP as corporate author with LBNL as publisher.

1. No currency or price year for any cost (only slag revenue is dated, 2006 USD). 2. Most figures are reprinted from 1990s sources (Farla 1998, Stelco 1993, NEDO 2008, vendor brochures) without restating the reference year or plant. 3. Cost bases are not stated (retrofit vs new, equipment vs installed). 4. Section 4.1.5 gives "about 70 kg/t" with no unit of what is recovered. 5. Sect. 1.1.1 NEDO figure refers to a "100 Mton-sinter/year plant", implausible plant size. 6. Sect. 9.2 increased electricity quoted in primary energy. 7. Heating-value basis stated only for the off-gas turbine (LHV). 8. Contents lists Appendix 1 (p.124) and Appendix 2 (p.138) that are absent from the PDF; sections 5.1 and 6 are headings only. 9. Commercial status is missing ("None provided") for FASTMET and BF charge distribution and blank for hot metal pretreatment.
